does: Presses a portion of rested kofte mixture between wet palms into a short, flat oval with a shallow dent from the thumb, so that it holds together over the fire and cooks fast and evenly, and is cooked afterwards on a grill or in a pan.

intro.what: This köfte method shapes rested mixture into flat ovals with a shallow thumb dent.
intro.why: It teaches you to control thickness and cohesion before the pieces meet the heat.

how: Keep a bowl of water beside the work and wet the hands lightly, so the mixture does not stick.
Take a portion about the size of a walnut and roll it once between the palms to bring it together.
Press it into a short oval, a little longer than it is wide, and flatten it so that it is the same thickness from end to end.
Press the thumb along the middle for a shallow dent, which keeps the middle from puffing up as it cooks.
Set the pieces on a tray, close in size, and keep them cool until they go on the heat.

cues.text: Each piece is an even, smooth oval with a shallow dent and no cracks at the edge.
The piece holds together when it is lifted and springs back a little when it is pressed.

mistakes.mistake: Shaping a mixture that was not worked or rested, so that the pieces crack and fall apart on the grill.
mistakes.fix: Knead it until sticky and let it rest in the cold before shaping.

mistakes.mistake: Making the pieces thick and round, so that the outside burns before the middle is done.
mistakes.fix: Flatten them to an even, modest thickness.

mistakes.mistake: Working with dry hands, so that the meat clings and tears.
mistakes.fix: Wet the hands lightly and often.

quiz.question: Why flatten the köfte evenly?
choices: To avoid a thick centre heating differently from the edges.
To make the centre deliberately thicker.
To remove the need to rest the mixture.
quiz.because: Even thickness reduces differences between the centre and edges during cooking.

quiz.question: What does the shallow thumb dent help control?
choices: The middle puffing up during cooking.
The mixture sticking to the hands.
quiz.because: A shallow central dent helps the oval retain a flatter shape as it cooks.

quiz.question: Which shape suggests well-formed flat köfte?
choices: Ragged ovals that split when lifted.
Smooth even ovals without edge cracks.
quiz.because: A smooth cohesive oval can be lifted while retaining its even thickness.

quiz.question: Pieces crack and fall apart during shaping. What should change?
choices: Work the mixture until sticky and let it rest cold.
Shape the loose mixture into larger portions.
Dry the hands and squeeze only the cracked edges.
quiz.because: Working and resting develops cohesion before individual pieces are formed.

comes_after.why: The mixture is worked until it is sticky and holds together before it is shaped.

variant_of.differs: The piece is pressed into a flat oval with a thumb dent and not rolled into a ball, and the mixture takes soaked bread as its binder. It is made to be cooked fast over fierce heat.
